t: Section 1022(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2004 (Public Law 108–136; 117 Stat. 1594; 10 U.S.C. 371 note), as most recently amended by section 1011 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013 (Public Law 112–239; 126 Stat. 1907) is amended by striking “2013” and inserting “2015”.

fable.w: This section only amends an earlier defense authorization provision by changing a date from 2013 to 2015, extending an existing authority. There is no tempting participation reading: it has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking mandate, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment that updates a fiscal year date in a previous statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with entities outside the federal government. It involves no public comment periods, advisory boards with non-federal members, or rights to sue.
qwen_block.s: Section 1022(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2004 ... is amended by striking “2013” and inserting “2015”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that only changes a date in an existing defense authority, apparently extending it to 2015. It does not set up any comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. No one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.
opus.s: is amended by striking “2013” and inserting “2015”.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** One tempting reading is that a provision amending a defense authority might bring in outsiders to a decision. It doesn't. This amendment only changes a date: it strikes "2013" and inserts "2015" in section 1022(b) of the FY2004 National Defense Authorization Act. That subsection appears to set when the authority ends, so this change seems to extend it by two years. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing or comment period, or given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment that updates a fiscal year reference in a previous statute. It does not create any mechanism for consultation, public comment, or participation by outside parties. It is purely a legislative correction and involves no interaction with non-federal entities regarding a decision.
qwen_chat.s: Section 1022(b) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2004 (Public Law 108–136; 117 Stat. 1594; 10 U.S.C. 371 note), as most recently amended by section 1011 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2013 (Public Law 112–239; 126 Stat. 1907) is amended by striking “2013” and inserting “2015”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that changing a date in a statute could imply a change in a consultation period or a deadline for public comment. However, the text is purely a technical amendment to a fiscal year reference in a previous law. It does not establish any process for outside parties to consult, comment, or participate in a decision. It is a legislative housekeeping measure.
